messages.subject: How to switch modelling zero to one and vice versa?
messages.subject_clean: How to switch modelling zero to one and vice versa?
messages.body_plain:
glmmTMB produces parameters estimates for probability of zero (absence). How we can find tha parameter estimates for the probability of 1 (Occurance)?

m1 <- glmmTMB(count~ mined,
              ziformula=~.,
              family=poisson, data=Salamanders)

Pred_m1=predict(m1, type="zprob")  ## gives probability of zero. But I want the parameter estimates so that I can predict 1 (non-zero) directly.

Thanks in advance for the help

messages.subject: possibility to evaluate the logL of a glmmTMB model with user-specified parameter values
messages.subject_clean: possibility to evaluate the logL of a glmmTMB model with user-specified parameter values
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Is there a convenient way to supply user-specified parameter values to a glmmTMB model to get the logLikelihood of the model with the user-specified parameter values?

e.g something like this:
glmmTMB(y ~ x+z+d+(1|Site),family=Poisson, parvalues = list(fixed, random))

Thanks a lot!

cheers, Bob Douma

messages.subject_clean: [TMB users] possibility to evaluate the logL of a glmmTMB model with user-specified parameter values
messages.body_plain:
I'll just point out the "where to ask about glmmTMB?" link is here:

https://github.com/glmmTMB/glmmTMB/#where-to-ask-questions

   Once you have fitted a model you can find the negative log-likelihood
function via $obj$fn() :

glmmTMB(formula = count ~ mined + (1 | site), data = Salamanders,
     family = poisson, ziformula = ~mined, dispformula = ~1)

names(m1$obj$par)
## [1] "beta"   "beta"   "betazi" "betazi" "theta"

  m1$obj$fn(c(1,1,0,0,1))
[1] 992.6808

messages.subject: speed with vectorization?
messages.body_plain:
Hi TMB users,

This is a very basic question, so I’m sorry if it’s been covered somewhere already. I couldn’t find the answer elsewhere.

Is there any speed improvement from replacing for-loops with vectorized operations? My first guess is that the answer is "no", based on the fact that the code to vectorize all the functions is written with for-loops (https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/TMB/inst/include/Vectorize.hpp), but there might be a complexity of compiling that I’m not aware of.

cheers,
Mollie

You are right: TMB vectorization doesn't offer speedups over for-loops. In fact, a manual for-loop may in theory be faster if you squeeze a lot of work into the body of the loop...

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: speed with vectorization?
messages.body_plain:
OK, I should have been a bit more specific on the vectorization comments:

Vectorization only affects a very tiny portion (say 1 percent) of a TMB model, i.e. the part that builds the computational graph.
Sure, you could make this part run faster but you would hardly notice a difference in overall runtime.

This is in contrast to Stan that builds the graph on each function evaluation. Here vectorization matters a lot.

Memorization is already being used by the current release of TMB, but future TMB versions will take even more advantage of memorization (caching of temporaries). If you are interested in the effect it has on glmmTMB try installing TMB from the branch 'TMB_experimental'.
